title: Flat coefficient push comparison from a bounded filtered module presentation
statement:
Fix the prime, field and separated finite-type scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $a:R\to S$ be a map of commutative condensed rings for which scalar extension is exact on every scheme. Write $T_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$, $U_Z$ for restriction, and $\gamma_f:T_YRf_{R*}\to Rf_{S*}T_X$ for [def-sfb-derived-push-hom]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories, identified with ring-sheaf module categories by [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison].
Let $I$ be a small nonempty filtered category and $(P_i)$ a diagram of flat $R_Y$-modules, with $f_R^*P_i$ flat, and an $R_Y$-linear colimit cocone $v_i:P_i\to U_YS_Y$. Let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$. For each $i$ let
$$\delta_i:Rf_{R*}K\otimes^L_{R_Y}P_i\longrightarrow Rf_{R*}(K\otimes^L_{R_X}f_R^*P_i)$$
be the canonical projection map, namely the adjunct of the pullback tensor comparison followed by $\varepsilon_K\otimes1$. If every $\delta_i$ is invertible, then $\gamma_{f,K}$ is invertible. More precisely, using tensor symmetry, restriction and $U_YRf_{S*}\cong Rf_{R*}U_X$, its composite with the cocone leg $1\otimes v_i$ equals $Rf_{R*}(1\otimes f_R^*v_i)\circ\delta_i$, using $f_R^*U_YS_Y\cong U_XS_X$.

source.place: paragraph (1), localization and filtered Qlbar arguments; former steps 2 and 4, canonical cocone legs

proof.text: Use the exact tensor and adjunction equivalences of [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] to work with ring-sheaf modules. Put $C=U_YS_Y$, $B=U_XS_X$, $L_R=f_R^*$, $L_S=f_S^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$ and $G_S=Rf_{S*}$. The coefficient morphisms of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] identify $f^{-1}R_Y=R_X$ and $f^{-1}S_Y=S_X$, compatibly with $a$, so $L_RC=B$. Pullback is exact for these arbitrary condensed coefficients by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main]. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], scalar restriction is exact and termwise on derived categories, and the scalar unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus $U_ZT_ZM=M\otimes^L_{R_Z}U_ZS_Z$, with scalar unit the tensor of $M$ with $R_Z\to U_ZS_Z$. This is the same scalar adjunction as for module objects: the relative tensor coequalizer and its adjunction of [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] send an $S$-linear map to its composite with $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; the monoidal equivalence preserves that coequalizer. Our flatness hypothesis makes $C$ and $B$ flat.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); identity-topos scalar extension and identified coefficient pullback

proof.text: The adjunction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] implies that the exact functor $L_R$ preserves the given colimit: maps from $L_RC$ to any module are, by adjunction, compatible families of maps from $P_i$ into its direct image. Hence $B=\varinjlim_i L_RP_i$, with legs $L_Rv_i$. Choose a complex $K^\bullet$ representing $K$ with $K^n=0$ for $n<a$. Flatness of each $L_RP_i$ and of $B$ means that tensoring is exact, so ordinary tensor with them preserves acyclic complexes (apply exactness to cycles and boundaries in every degree). These degree-zero modules are therefore K-flat. It follows that $K^\bullet\otimes L_RP_i$ and $K^\bullet\otimes B$ represent the corresponding derived tensors and vanish below $a$. By [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor], their termwise colimit is $K^\bullet\otimes B$, with the specified tensor legs. On $Y$, the same result applied to a K-flat representative $A^\bullet$ of $G_RK$, available by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], gives $A^\bullet\otimes C=\varinjlim_i(A^\bullet\otimes P_i)$, representing $G_RK\otimes^L C$ and $G_RK\otimes^L P_i$. Exact filtered colimits commute with cohomology: cycles and boundaries are preserved since their defining kernel, image and cokernel sequences are exact.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to the strict diagram $K^\bullet\otimes L_RP_i$. Its index is small and filtered, its terms have the single lower bound $a$, its coefficients are precisely $R_X=p_X^*R$, and $f$ is qcqs. Step 2 identifies its termwise colimit with $K\otimes^L B$. Consequently, for every $q$ the maps induced by $G_R(1\otimes L_Rv_i)$ identify $H^qG_R(K\otimes^L B)$ with $\varinjlim_iH^qG_R(K\otimes^L L_RP_i)$. Step 2 likewise identifies $H^q(G_RK\otimes^L C)$ with $\varinjlim_iH^q(G_RK\otimes^L P_i)$. These are comparisons with the actual cocone maps, rather than choices of isomorphisms between the endpoints.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1), and proof of the cohomology comparison (5.4)

proof.text: Let $d:U_YG_S\xrightarrow{\sim}G_RU_X$ and $b:U_XL_S\xrightarrow{\sim}L_RU_Y$ be the comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. The map $d$ is the restriction comparison used in [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso]: both derive the identical underived restriction/pushforward composite of [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso], and restriction preserves K-injectives by [lem-sfb-comap-preserves-k-injectives]. On a K-injective $S_X$-complex both are the identity under that underived identification. Consider the two factorizations from $(X,S_X)$ to $(Y,R_Y)$, through $(Y,S_Y)$ and through $(X,R_X)$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] to this commutative ringed square, with the identity-topos ring changes on its scalar edges. It identifies the conjugate of $d$ with the canonical composition comparison $\theta:L_ST_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_XL_R$. Under restriction and $b$, this comparison is the tensor/pullback comparison $\mu_{M,C}:L_R(M\otimes^L C)\to L_RM\otimes^L B$. Indeed, on flat-term K-flat representatives both are the sheafified tensor associator: the inverse-image section of $m\otimes s$ maps to the inverse-image section of $m$ tensored with the coefficient image of $s$. The scalar units of Step 1 insert $1$, so the unit normalizations agree; the tensor compatibility asserted in the cited square lemma gives the same comparison after localization.

By [def-sfb-derived-push-hom], $\gamma$ is the coefficient mate formed from this $d$. Apply the general categorical assertion [lem-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-push-counit], with all four object predicates identically true, the two geometric adjunctions $L_R\dashv G_R$, $L_S\dashv G_S$, and the scalar adjunctions $T_Z\dashv U_Z$. It says that the geometric adjoint of $\gamma_K$ is $T_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\circ\theta_{G_RK}$. The adjoint compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] therefore says that the $R$-geometric adjoint of $h=d_{T_XK}\circ U_Y(\gamma_K)$ is $U_XT_X(\varepsilon^R_K)\circ U_X(\theta_{G_RK})\circ b_{T_YG_RK}^{-1}$. By Step 4 and the tensor identification of Step 1 this is exactly $(\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1_B)\circ\mu_{G_RK,C}$. Thus $h$ is the projection map $\delta_C$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. This proves equality of the specified morphisms, with the tensor symmetry used to place the coefficient on the right.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); coefficient mate and its geometric transpose

proof.text: The projection map in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] is natural in its coefficient argument. Apply it to the $R_Y$-linear map $v_i:P_i\to C$. This gives $\delta_C\circ(1\otimes v_i)=G_R(1\otimes L_Rv_i)\circ\delta_i$. Explicitly, taking $L_R\dashv G_R$ adjoints gives on both sides $\varepsilon^R_K\otimes L_Rv_i$ after the pullback tensor comparison; its naturality makes these adjoints equal. Step 5 replaces $\delta_C$ with $d\circ U_Y\gamma_K$. This is the asserted cocone-leg formula. Applying the same naturality to each diagram arrow shows that the $\delta_i$ form a morphism of the two stage diagrams.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), naturality of its counit definition

proof.text: For every $q$, use the two cohomology-colimit identifications of Step 3. The identity in Step 6 identifies $H^q(h)$ with the map induced by the compatible family $H^q(\delta_i)$: the cohomology cocone legs are jointly epimorphic by the universal property of the sheaf colimit. Each stage map is invertible by hypothesis, and the stage inverses form a compatible family by multiplying the naturality squares by the inverses. Taking colimits gives an inverse to $H^q(h)$. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism in the derived category, whose inverted morphisms are the quasi-isomorphisms. Since $d$ is an isomorphism and $U_Y$ reflects isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], $\gamma_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism. Only cohomology-colimit detection is used here; no claim that arbitrary filtered diagrams have their colimits in the ordinary triangulated category is required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q30-2e4f845b6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full 7-step split and every cited statement. Statement unchanged from the base; the only stmt_deps addition is sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms, which the statement uses implicitly. No new nodes. Step 1: the exact monoidal comparison and the scalar adjunction units agree; C and B are flat because scalar extension is exact. Step 2: L_R is a left adjoint, so it preserves the module colimit; a flat degree-0 module is K-flat; the termwise Tot colimit comes from lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity fits (condensed Λ_X, common lower bound, canonical maps) and matches HRS Lemma 5.3(1) and (5.4); Remark 5.4 shows why the statement needs K in D+. Step 4: the ringed-square lemma's c is d of lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction, which matches def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso on K-injectives; θ restricts to μ, checked on flat K-flat representatives where everything is underived. Step 5: the push-counit lemma with all predicates true and e=d (orientation checked against def-sfb-mate-push-hom), plus the adjoint compatibility, gives d∘Uγ = α_C as specified maps. Steps 6–7: naturality in P gives the leg formula; on cohomology the map is a colimit of isomorphisms; restriction reflects isomorphisms. Small cases checked: R=S (identity), the citer's O_E→E and Qbar presentations, zero coefficients. Route: the continuity node's unit sk-thm-properbasechange is in the unit's uses. Advisory only: det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image (sk-cor-pe-bounded-continuity) is the blueprint's literal citation. No SGA; no duplicate (lem-sfb-coefficient-projection-square is a different statement); no cycle; tool_uses accepted.
